column3: The Hebrew says the king’s heart was “toward Absalom”; BSB makes the longing explicit.
The Hebrew says that Joab took a woman from there; BSB presents bringing her as the purpose of his sending.
The Hebrew begins with the woman speaking to the king; BSB says that she went to him.
The Hebrew calls it “my ember that remains”; BSB adds “one.”
The Hebrew has an active plural clause, “they will not destroy my son”; BSB expresses it passively. BSB also supplies “head” in the promise about the hair.
The Hebrew says “his banished one”; BSB supplies “son.”
The Hebrew says “to hear the good and the evil”; BSB uses “discern good and evil.”
The Hebrew repeats the image of putting words into her mouth; BSB says that Joab told her exactly what to say.
The Hebrew says “turn the face of the matter”; BSB renders the image as bringing about a change of affairs.
The Hebrew says “I have done this thing”; BSB uses “I hereby grant this request.”
The Hebrew shifts from “your servant” to “I have found favor”; BSB maintains the third person.
The Hebrew says that he did not see “the king’s face”; BSB shortens this to seeing the king.
The Hebrew says “according to the king’s stone”; BSB renders the weight image as “according to the royal standard.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Absalom at the beginning; BSB uses “he.”
